scenes.say: Ever get stuck on Windows and wish you had your favorite Linux commands? Let’s match up the tools so you’re never lost.

scenes.label: ipconfig
scenes.sub: Like 'ip a' on Linux, shows all IP addresses and adapters.
scenes.say: To check network details, use ipconfig. It’s the Windows version of the ip address command.

scenes.title: Find process on port 443
scenes.say: Want to know which process owns a port? Get-NetTCPConnection shows you the process ID, then Get-Process reveals the name.
If a server’s slow, check Task Manager first, then Resource Monitor for deeper stats. Perfmon tracks disk and CPU bottlenecks.

scenes.question: How do you find which process owns port 443?
scenes.wrong: Just use netstat and guess the PID.
scenes.right: Get-NetTCPConnection shows the process ID; Get-Process names it.
scenes.say: Don’t just guess the process. Use Get-NetTCPConnection for the ID, then Get-Process to see the actual name.
